items.title: Census 2011 — Key Figures at a Glance
items.body:
Census 2011 was the **15th** census of India and the **7th** since Independence. The census began under **Lord Mayo (1872)** and became regular decennial from **1881**; the first modern census anywhere was Sweden (1749). Commissioner: **C. Chandramouli**. Motto: **"Our Census, Our Future"**. Conducted in two phases — **House-listing (Apr-Sep 2010)** and **Population Enumeration (9-28 Feb 2011)** — by the Registrar General & Census Commissioner under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Total population | 121 crore (1,210,569,573) |
| Males / Females | 62.3 cr / 58.7 cr |
| Decadal growth (2001-11) | 17.7% (absolute +18.19 cr) |
| Density | 382 persons/km2 |
| Sex ratio (all ages) | 943 |
| Child sex ratio (0-6) | 919 |
| Literacy | 74.04% |
| Rural : Urban | 68.8% : 31.2% |
| SC / ST share | 16.6% / 8.6% |

Administrative units covered: **640 districts, 5,924 sub-districts, 7,936 towns, ~6.4 lakh villages**.
keyPoints: Census 2011 = 15th census overall, 7th after Independence; census began 1872 (Mayo), regular from 1881.
Motto 'Our Census, Our Future'; Commissioner C. Chandramouli; conducted under Ministry of Home Affairs.
Total population 121 crore; density 382/km2; decadal growth 17.7% (absolute increase 18.19 crore).
Sex ratio 943 (all ages), child sex ratio 919 (0-6 yrs); literacy 74.04%.
Rural 68.8% : Urban 31.2%; SC 16.6% and ST 8.6% of population.
items.mnemonic: Big four of 2011: '121-382-943-74' = population 121 cr, density 382, sex ratio 943, literacy 74%.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Geography: Census 2011

items.title: Sex Ratio, Child Sex Ratio & Literacy
items.body:
## Sex ratio (females per 1000 males)

- National **943** (up from 933 in 2001). **Rural 949 > Urban 929**.
- Highest: **Kerala 1084**, Puducherry 1037; **Andhra Pradesh 993** (4th). Lowest: **Haryana**.
- **Child sex ratio (0-6)** fell from **976 (1961) to 919 (2011)** — an alarming decline; worst **Haryana (793)**, best **Arunachal Pradesh/Mizoram/Kerala**. In 1991-2001 the child ratio dropped below the overall ratio for the first time.

## Literacy (age 7+, read & write with understanding)

- National **74.04%** (2001: 64.83%). **Male 82.14%, Female 65.46%** — gap **16.68 pts**.
- Highest state **Kerala (94%)**, lowest **Bihar (61.8%)**; best district **Serchhip (Mizoram)**, worst **Alirajpur (MP)**.
- SC literacy 66.1%, ST literacy 59% — both below the national average.
keyPoints: Sex ratio 943 (rural 949 > urban 929); highest Kerala 1084, lowest Haryana; AP 993.
Child sex ratio (0-6) declined 976 (1961) to 919 (2011); lowest Haryana (793).
Literacy 74.04% — male 82.14%, female 65.46%, gender gap 16.68 percentage points.
Highest literacy Kerala (94%), lowest Bihar (61.8%); SC 66.1%, ST 59%.
In 1991-2001 the child sex ratio fell below the overall sex ratio for the first time.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Geography: Census 2011; World Geography: Demography

items.title: Population Growth, Age Structure & Demographic Transition
items.body:
## Growth landmarks

- **1911-1921** — only decade of **negative growth (-0.03%)**, due to the 1918-19 influenza epidemic.
- **1921** — 'Great Divide'/demographic turning point (death rates began falling).
- **1961-1971** — decade of **maximum growth (24.8%)**; **1951-1981** = 'population explosion'.
- Decadal growth has fallen since 1981; 2001-11 was **17.7%**.

## Age structure & demographic dividend

- 0-14 yrs fell **42% (1971) to 29% (2011)**; working-age 15-59 rose to **63% (2011)**; 60+ rose to **8%**.
- A large working-age bulge (15-64) relative to dependants = the **demographic dividend** — an economic-growth opportunity.

## Demographic Transition Theory

| Stage | Birth rate | Death rate | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | High | High | Low/stagnant |
| II | High | Falling | Rapid (explosion) |
| III | Low | Low | Low/stable |

India is broadly in **late Stage II / early Stage III** (TFR near replacement 2.1 in many states). **Malthus** held population grows geometrically while food grows arithmetically.
keyPoints: 1911-1921 was the only decade of negative growth (influenza epidemic).
1961-1971 saw maximum decadal growth (24.8%); 1951-1981 = population explosion.
0-14 age share fell 42% (1971) to 29% (2011); 15-59 rose to 63% — basis of the demographic dividend.
Demographic Transition: Stage I high birth/death, Stage II falling death (rapid growth), Stage III low/stable.
Malthus: population grows geometrically, food arithmetically.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — World Geography: Demography

items.title: Migration, Distribution & Settlement Patterns
items.body:
## Migration

- **Internal streams:** rural-to-rural (largest, mainly women via marriage), rural-to-urban, urban-to-urban, urban-to-rural.
- **Push factors:** unemployment, poverty, disasters, unrest. **Pull factors:** jobs, security, better services.
- **Net Migration Rate** = immigrants - emigrants per 1000. Marriage is the leading reason for female migration; work/employment for males.

## Distribution & density

- World: **>90% of people live on ~10% of land**; controlling factors are geographical (water, landforms, climate, soils), economic (minerals, urbanisation, industry) and socio-cultural.
- Density = persons per km2 (India 382; most populous state **Uttar Pradesh**; UT density max **Delhi**, min **Andaman & Nicobar**).

## Settlement patterns

- **Rural:** nucleated/clustered, dispersed/scattered, semi-clustered, hamleted.
- **Urban hierarchy:** town -> city -> **million-plus city** -> metropolis (>1 million) -> **megacity (>10 million)**. Class-I towns have 1 lakh+.
keyPoints: Internal migration streams: rural-rural (largest), rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural.
Push = unemployment/disasters/unrest; Pull = jobs/security/services; marriage drives female migration.
Over 90% of world population lives on about 10% of the land.
Rural settlement types: nucleated, dispersed, semi-clustered, hamleted.
Urban hierarchy: metropolis > 1 million, megacity > 10 million; Class-I town = 1 lakh+.

items.title: Tribes of India & Andhra Pradesh (incl. PVTGs)
items.body:
## Scheduled Tribes

- ST = **8.6%** of India (2011). Highest ST share among states: **Mizoram/Nagaland**; largest ST numbers: **Madhya Pradesh**; Andaman-N&N and few others have distinct groups.
- Major tribes: **Gond, Bhil, Santhal** (largest tribes of India), Munda, Oraon, Naga.

## Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)

- **75 PVTGs** in India across **18 states + 1 UT** — identified on criteria of pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, stagnant/declining population and geographical isolation.
- **Andhra Pradesh (undivided) had 12 PVTGs:** **Chenchu** (best-known, Nallamala/NSTR), **Konda Reddi**, **Konda Savara**, **Bodo Gadaba**, **Gutob Gadaba**, **Dongria Khond**, **Kutia Khond**, **Bondo Porja**, **Khond Porja**, **Kolam**, **Thoti**, and Kondasavara.

## AP tribes (Scheduled Tribes)

- Prominent AP STs: **Yanadi** (largest, Nellore region), **Koya, Savara (Sugalis/Lambadis), Konda Dora, Gadaba, Chenchu**. Concentrated in the **Eastern Ghats** (Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam) and Nallamala.
keyPoints: ST = 8.6% of India (2011); Gond, Bhil and Santhal are the largest tribes.
India has 75 PVTGs across 18 states and 1 UT.
Chenchu is the best-known PVTG of Andhra Pradesh (Nallamala / Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam).
Undivided AP had 12 PVTGs incl. Chenchu, Konda Reddi, Konda Savara, Bodo/Gutob Gadaba, Dongria/Kutia Khond, Bondo/Khond Porja, Kolam, Thoti.
Yanadi is AP's largest Scheduled Tribe (Nellore region); tribes concentrate in the Eastern Ghats and Nallamala.
items.source: Ministry of Tribal Affairs — PVTG scheme; en.wikipedia.org PVTG list (verified Sep 2026); AP Tribal Welfare Dept

items.title: AP Demographics, Population Policy & the 2027 Census
items.body:
## Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011, residuary state)

- Population **~4.94 crore** (post-bifurcation) — ~4.09% of India; **10th** most populous.
- **Sex ratio 993** (well above national 943 — among the best); **density ~304/km2** (below national 382).
- Literacy **~67%** (below national 74%); high urbanisation on the coast; SC ~17%, ST ~5.5%.

## Population policy

- India was the **first country** to adopt an official family-planning policy (**1952**).
- **National Population Policy 2000** — goal of **replacement-level fertility (TFR 2.1)** and population stabilisation by 2045; supported by NHP 2017, Mission Parivar Vikas, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, PCPNDT Act (1994).

## Census 2027 (16th census)

- India's **first fully digital census** with an **optional self-enumeration** portal (16 languages) and **caste enumeration** for the first time since 1931.
- Two phases: **House-listing Apr-Sep 2026**; **Population Enumeration 9-28 Feb 2027**. Reference date **00:00 of 1 March 2027** (for snow-bound Ladakh/J&K/HP/Uttarakhand, PE is Sep 2026 with reference **1 Oct 2026**). It will feed the next **delimitation** exercise.
keyPoints: AP (2011, residuary): population ~4.94 cr, sex ratio 993 (above national), density ~304, literacy ~67%.
India was the first country to adopt an official family-planning policy (1952).
National Population Policy 2000 targets replacement-level fertility (TFR 2.1).
Census 2027 is the 16th census, India's first digital census, with caste enumeration (first since 1931).
Census 2027 reference date is 1 March 2027 (1 Oct 2026 for snow-bound regions); it feeds delimitation.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey / Census 2011; National Population Policy 2000; PIB & en.wikipedia.org 2027 Census of India (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: World Regional Geography — Canals, Isthmuses, Rivers, Lakes, Capitals & Peoples
items.body:
## Canals & isthmuses

| Feature | Links / location |
|---|---|
| Suez Canal (1869) | Mediterranean-Red Sea; Egypt; sea-level, no locks |
| Panama Canal (1914) | Atlantic-Pacific; uses locks |
| Kiel Canal | North Sea-Baltic Sea; Germany |
| Isthmus of Panama | joins North & South America |
| Isthmus of Suez | joins Africa & Asia |
| Isthmus of Kra | narrow neck of the Malay Peninsula (Thailand) |

## Rivers & the capitals on them

- Thames-**London**, Seine-**Paris**, Tiber-**Rome**, Danube-**Vienna/Budapest/Belgrade**, Moskva-**Moscow**, Nile-**Cairo**, Tigris-**Baghdad**, Potomac-**Washington D.C.**
- Nile = longest river; Amazon = greatest volume; Danube = Europe's 2nd-longest.

## Major lakes

- **Caspian Sea** = largest lake (area); **Superior** = largest freshwater lake (area); **Baikal** = deepest & largest by volume; **Victoria** = largest in Africa; **Titicaca** = highest navigable; **Dead Sea** = lowest & among the saltiest.

## Countries & capitals that trip candidates

- Australia -> **Canberra** (not Sydney); Canada -> **Ottawa** (not Toronto); Brazil -> **Brasilia** (not Rio); Turkey -> **Ankara** (not Istanbul); USA -> **Washington D.C.**

## Peoples of the world

| People | Region |
|---|---|
| Kirghiz | Central Asian steppes |
| Maori | New Zealand |
| Lapps (Sami) | Arctic Scandinavia |
| Tuareg | Sahara Desert |
| Mongols | Gobi Desert |
| Bindibu / Aborigines | Australian deserts |
| Eskimo (Inuit) | Arctic tundra |
keyPoints: Suez Canal (Mediterranean-Red Sea, no locks) and Panama Canal (Atlantic-Pacific, with locks) are the key ship canals; Kiel links the North Sea and Baltic.
The Isthmus of Panama joins North & South America; the Isthmus of Suez joins Africa & Asia; the Isthmus of Kra is in Thailand.
Capitals on rivers: London-Thames, Paris-Seine, Cairo-Nile, Baghdad-Tigris, Rome-Tiber.
Caspian Sea = largest lake; Baikal = deepest; Superior = largest freshwater by area; Victoria = largest in Africa; Titicaca = highest navigable.
Non-obvious capitals: Canberra (Australia), Ottawa (Canada), Brasilia (Brazil), Ankara (Turkey).
Peoples: Kirghiz (Central Asian steppes), Maori (New Zealand), Lapps/Sami (Arctic), Tuareg (Sahara), Mongols (Gobi).
items.mnemonic: Canals: 'Suez-no-locks, Panama-locks'; lakes: 'Caspian biggest, Baikal deepest'.
items.source: NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography / India: Physical Environment; Goh Cheng Leong; standard world atlas (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: Tribe–State Mapping (All-India, UPSC-style)
items.body:
## Match-the-following: tribe ↔ home state

| Tribe | State / Region |
|---|---|
| **Limboo (Limbu)** | **Sikkim** |
| **Dongaria Kondh** (PVTG) | **Odisha** (Niyamgiri hills) |
| **Karbi** | **Assam** (NOT Himachal Pradesh) |
| **Bonda** (PVTG) | **Odisha** (NOT Tamil Nadu) |
| **Bhotia / Lepcha** | Sikkim–north Bengal |
| **Toda** | Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu |
| **Chenchu** (PVTG) | Andhra Pradesh–Telangana (Nallamala) |

- These pairings recur in prelims match items; the classic traps are placing **Karbi** in HP (it is Assam) and **Bonda** in Tamil Nadu (it is Odisha).
keyPoints: Limboo (Limbu) is a tribe of Sikkim.
Dongaria Kondh (a PVTG) live in the Niyamgiri hills of Odisha.
Karbi are of Assam, not Himachal Pradesh.
Bonda (a PVTG) are of Odisha, not Tamil Nadu.
Chenchu (PVTG) belong to the Nallamala region of Andhra Pradesh–Telangana.
items.source: Census of India / Ministry of Tribal Affairs (verified Sep 2026)
